text: Dallas, in partnership with Sandia National Laboratories, is the host of the NAWEA/WindTech 2025 Conference in Dallas and the facilities and equipment procured by this project will be featured to conference participants. The renovated facility provides the potential for research and educational expansion into other energy sources, storm predictions, and/or support research in aeronautical engineering. This project delivered critical equipment and physical infrastructure to enable the Center for Wind Energy to achieve excellence by creating a place where academia works in partnership with students, industry and civic leaders to advance existing and future applications of wind engineering. Scope of Work The designated space for the Center for Wind Energy is located in a building on campus called the “Waterview Science and Technology Center” (WSTC). This building houses our Boundary Layer and Subsonic wind Tunnel. For the renovations, we have converted existing but unused lab and office space in WSTC to have the following: • Intelligent Energy Systems Lab, which hosts an “electronics shop” plus student space with computer workstations. In this lab staff and students can perform prototyping and testing for diagnostics and control of wind turbine components. The lab also hosts workstations that run software for numerical simulation and design of wind energy systems such as codes developed by NREL (e.g., WISDEM, OpenFAST, FLORIS, FAST.Farm, WindSE and others) as well as Matlab/Simulink, machine learning codes and productivity software. Cubicles for students and postdocs were designed and placed in this lab space. • Space renovation required for new wind/wave tunnel. UTD acquired (with its own funds) a brand-new wind/water-wave tunnel (WWT) to expand the center's research, educational and outreach infrastructure. However, there was no space that can fit the WWT facility (which has a test section of approximately 9 m long, 1 m wide, and 2 m high). We therefore used the project funds to renovate two rooms to accommodate the new WWT. • Conference room for meetings with existing industry partners, recruiting new partners and the relevant staff. Offices for the Center leadership, faculty, staff members and visiting scientists/engineers. • Reception lobby to Center that serves as the entrance and reception area for visitors, clients, and employees. It plays a crucial role in creating a positive first impression and setting the tone for the entire office environment. For equipment, the project called for the acquisition and integration of: • Circuit, transducer and actuator testing equipment (e.g., power supplies, oscilloscopes, multi‐ channel data acquisition systems and standard tools, etc.) and benches to support workstations in the “electronics shop”. • Wind tunnel metrology/sensors and data acquisition systems for testing the effects of air moving past fixed and rotating solid objects. • Dedicated data storage to handle terabytes of data generated from computer simulations and experiments from the wind tunnel and other relevant labs conducting research in energy. This project aimed to renovate an existing facility to create a modern, functional and collaborative environment that supports the Center’s needs and enhances the productivity and efficiency of the staff and students.
